resources.string:
Android only lets an app cover the status bar as an accessibility service.

On the next screen, open "LiteLauncher top bar" and turn it on. It reads nothing on your screen.

If Android says the setting is restricted (Android 13 and newer, for apps not installed from a store): open Settings → Apps → LiteLauncher Top Bar, tap ⋮ → "Allow restricted settings", then try again.

Showing the top bar in all apps needs the small "LiteLauncher Top Bar" add-on (litelauncher-topbar.apk, next to the launcher's APK).

It's a separate app because it uses an accessibility service (the only way an app may draw over the status bar), and Google Play Protect blocks downloaded apps that have one. To install it anyway, either:

• Temporarily turn off Play Store → your profile → Play Protect → ⚙ → "Scan apps with Play Protect", install the add-on, then turn it back on; or
• Install it from a computer with: adb install litelauncher-topbar.apk

Then choose this menu item again.
Turn off \"LiteLauncher top bar\" in Accessibility settings
